Blocks.Text: RolltheSpire2 1.4.0
This page summarizes the main changes and scope of version 1.4.0.
This version gives RT2 a thorough round of refinement: a reorganized interface and encyclopedia, more search conditions, and prediction that starts to follow the actions and routes of an actual run.

After upgrading from 1.3.5, setting conditions, finding seeds, viewing results and saving them will still feel familiar. What has changed is the interface you open, the ways you can express what you want, and the help available for understanding conditions and results.
A refined night-blue interface
The main panel now uses a consistent night-blue palette, with reworked fonts, object images and text, selection states, spacing and page hierarchy.
Page preparation and long lists have also been adjusted to reduce the burden of repeated creation and concentrated refreshes.
I hope it can accommodate more complex needs while making everyday use more comfortable.
Encyclopedia: explaining the thinking behind the design
Several encyclopedia articles have been rewritten in this round.
The existing explanations of mechanics remain, with more concrete player needs, situations and trade-offs. For example:

Items: Why are the rewards specified in a search treated as choices you intend to make?
Why can taking one extra card sometimes change the final curse from Neow’s Bones?
Why does an event’s position in the queue not guarantee which question-mark room will contain it?
Why does map search use different properties and route requirements instead of one universal “good map score”?
Which needs suit high-speed seed search, and which processes are better handed to a predictor after you see the actual map?

Blocks.Text: These questions concern both what RT2 is trying to solve and how its results should be used. I hope the encyclopedia can do more than help you fill in conditions: it should explain where they come from and the balance between freedom of expression, correct results, required input and computation cost.
Library and reusable card collections
The Seed Library has become the [b]Library[/b], adding independently saved card collections alongside favorites, presets and history.

You can create a collection spanning multiple characters, filter cards by name or ID, character/card pool, rarity and type, add or remove cards continuously, and save, edit, copy or delete collections.
Card collections currently serve two purposes:

Items: [b]Search exclusions[/b]: require the initial card rewards from the first 1–6 normal combats checked after the opening to contain no collection members.
[b]Route highlights[/b]: choose collections you care about in the in-run route overview to find relevant cards along the way.

Blocks.Text: A query saves a snapshot of the collection’s members when you select it. Editing or deleting the source collection later does not silently change saved queries. You can explicitly update them when you want the newer version.

Route prediction also remembers your chosen collections. It highlights all Rare cards by default, while retaining the complete rewards. Changing highlights does not change your route or take rewards for you.
More specific search conditions
Standard single-player searches can now target relics in the first chest, second chest, or either of the first two chests.

Chests are counted in the order actually encountered, including those generated by question-mark rooms. The corresponding single-player Seed Information display now shows chest relics in a nine-slot sequence.
Ordinary Act 1 question-mark rooms also have a prefix condition: require the first few ordinary question-mark rolls to produce events.
Map search: arrange the route you want
The map page retains the three-Act total and per-Act entries. Common count objectives and independent map properties have been rearranged, with direct number input and plus/minus controls.

Each Act now has a [b]drawing mode[/b]. Drag or append Monster, Unknown, Shop, Elite and Rest nodes to the axis in the order you want to encounter them. Box-select nodes into a group when their internal order does not matter.
For example, you can ask for:
Visit an Elite and a Rest Site in either order, then a Shop, then another Elite.

These requirements must all be satisfied by [b]one complete route[/b], with extra rooms allowed along the way. Fixed opening Monsters, fixed chests and the pre-Boss Rest Site do not automatically count toward the manually drawn requirements.
Faster complete generation and an optional lossy prefilter
Map search continues to use complete evaluation by default, with less repeated exploration and temporary workspace use during complete map generation.
There is also a [b]lossy prefilter, off by default[/b], using the CPU or GPU for supported vanilla standard single-player conditions.

[b]The lossy prefilter can miss seeds that meet your requirements.[/b] Remaining candidates still undergo complete map evaluation. Broad conditions may not benefit from prefiltering; choose according to your needs.
In-run operation prediction: compare the consequences of choices
Supported native options, rewards, relics, shops, transformations and potions can show predicted outcomes from the current state.
This also explores deeper sequences of choices:

Items: [b]Reroll groups and order previews[/b]: inspect subsequent rerolls in the current reward set, including different reroll orders in situations such as Colorful Philosophers.
[b]Multiple sacrifice previews[/b]: use your current Pael’s Wing progress to see relics obtainable by continuing to sacrifice these rewards.
[b]Effects after acquisition[/b]: distinguish intermediate choices, automatic acquisition and later outcomes in supported situations.
[b]Complex shop restocks[/b]: when a purchase also requires card selection or another transaction, continue inspecting restocks and some related effects under the stated assumptions.
[b]Post-combat rewards in specific events[/b]: preview rewards after choosing combat, under explicit combat-resolution assumptions.

Blocks.Text: Potion previews now show use order, letting you compare what a potion will do after other potions are used first. They usually expand through the third use. If more than eight groups would be shown, the entire preview returns to two layers. Potion icons retain the order while keeping the display manageable.

Each prediction has its own supported sources, stages and assumptions. Operation prediction has an independent switch and per-source display controls. When RandomForeseer is also installed, Auto mode yields some duplicate basic displays while retaining RT2’s additional information.
Route prediction for the current Act

On the map during an actual run, use the native pen, right-click drawing and eraser tools to express the route you want through the current Act, then inspect encounters, events, shops and rewards along it.

Card selections, skips, event branches and purchases at nodes feed into later predictions. Change a choice and the subsequent outcomes are recalculated. As you advance in the real run, predictions continue from the actual progress and state.

Route prediction currently focuses on [b]the actual current Act in single-player[/b]. Combat outcomes still have stated assumptions; it does not simulate the sequence of card plays in a whole battle. Your actual choices and additional random consumption during normal play can also change later outcomes.
Further improvements to the Crystal Sphere assistant
The existing Crystal Sphere assistant has further refinements to target combinations, gold plans and reveal guidance:

Items: Find gold-oriented plans even when no card or other reward targets are selected.
Continue considering compatible gold gains when reward targets are retained.
Distinguish the completion states of candidate evaluation, feasible plans and proof of maximum gold.
Keep verified plans while continuing to search unresolved questions.
Reduce repeated computation and display work with complex relic states.

Blocks.Text: Proof of optimal gold and completion of the candidate list are handled separately. Finishing one does not mark the other complete.
Search execution, compatibility and saved results

CPU batch prescreening, opening random calculations, reward-pool preparation, candidate-identity reuse, GPU batch submission and data transfer have received targeted optimizations to reduce repeated work on applicable paths.

Automatic execution order uses clearer computation-cost references, with transfer time and complete-call time handled separately. Benefits vary with the query, device and startup state. Rarity and predicted time remain estimates.
Manual adjustment of family execution order
Before starting, you can inspect the automatic order or switch to manual mode and move filter families up or down. The search then runs in the order you selected.

If you know these families, or simply want to try how different orders affect search performance, you can adjust them, inspect actual runtime readings, and switch back to automatic ordering. Missing time estimates do not prevent manual execution.
Result handling is also clearer

Items: [b]Confirmed results[/b] satisfy the conditions in the final model check.
[b]Unverified candidates[/b] retain the scope and reasons the model cannot yet confirm. They can be saved and checked again later.
[b]Actual execution failures[/b] retain their original causes and pending work instead of being treated as conditions not matching.

Blocks.Text: Within trustworthy recovery boundaries, independent seeds can continue to be processed. Auxiliary problems in saving, estimates, display and cleanup are kept separate from search computation where possible. Favorites, history, condition restoration and reuse after restart have also received further workflow validation.

Fixed incorrect random-state rotation calculations in some GPU environments by using an equivalent rotation implementation with two 32-bit halves. This may improve some Neow’s Bones searches that return no usable candidates or miss matching seeds.

The GPU has additional applicable numerical compatibility paths, while retaining initialization causes and an explicit retry entry. Devices, operating systems, game updates and rule-changing mods can still affect execution or accuracy. Concrete feedback and logs remain important.
Other changes

Items: Settings are organized into Features, Preferences, Advanced and Diagnostics. In-run tool entry points, operation prediction and map routes have separate controls.
A new explicit single-player in-run Test Console supports finding and adding objects, adjusting decks or potions, and entering events and encounters for experiments and issue reproduction.
Improved registered content names, external card art and presentation alongside some other mods.
Consolidated repeated internal checks and mechanic facts to reduce the risk of inconsistent maintenance changes.
About now includes a permanent Contributors & acknowledgements chapter.

Blocks.Text: Acknowledgements
Thank you, [b]James Zhou (@JamesZhou233)[/b].

James shared and discussed GPU execution and data-transfer optimizations with me earlier, providing concrete implementations and comparison material. This work helped RT2 improve batch submission, buffer reuse and candidate data transfer. The ideas were then independently adapted to the current version’s execution and recovery behavior.
[url=https://github.com/FalseOcean/rollthespire2/pull/4]See James’s optimization proposal and PR[/url]
Thank you, [b]Egoistic今宵 (@shion0528)[/b].

His CPU/GPU filtering and opening-simulation optimizations, benchmarks and validation material provided valuable references for batch prescreening, random-computation reuse, reward-pool preparation and candidate-state reuse. After adaptation and validation for the current version, these methods entered applicable search paths.
[url=https://github.com/shion0528/rollthespire2/releases/tag/v1.3.5-resource.17]See shion’s research version and implementation[/url]

Both started from the public 1.3.5, studied it carefully, and returned to discuss their own implementations, giving RT2 opportunities to keep improving. I am grateful for that help, and for the players who shared real experiences, seeds, saves and logs during this round.
